title: Sihti2: noise writes a diffusion geometry
summary: Sihti2 takes Sihti's operator-defined persistence into a null-input regime. IID colour noise writes a heterogeneous local conductance graph and the same signal is then propagated through that graph. The branch reframes the boxy late states as candidate metastable / almost-invariant diffusion domains and turns the visual clue into measurable questions about graph bottlenecks, mixing time, heat trace and spectral dimension. The repo explicitly fences the interpretation: persistent domains are not semantic objects, and fractal / Griffiths language is not earned without finite-size and scaling evidence.

nodes.claim: Turns Sihti's noise observation into a random-conductance spectral-geometry program with matched self, independent-geometry, shuffled-conductance and blank-lattice controls.
nodes.survived: The exact implemented object is a lazy reversible diffusion on a graph whose conductances are written by the input; the experiment now measures Laplacian gap/relaxation, stationary-measure variance, edge disagreement, heat trace and effective spectral-dimension slopes rather than reading objecthood from appearance.
nodes.killed: No semantic-object, fractal, renormalization-group or Griffiths-phase claim is accepted from a compelling late image alone; those interpretations require stable scaling, finite-size controls and matched nulls.

edges.why: Sihti2 explicitly starts from Sihti's IID-noise own-EQ observation and keeps the same image-written conductance / lazy-diffusion mechanism while changing the research question from object placement to spectral geometry and metastability.
